# TensorsLab Vision Skills

> Open-source, executable AI-agent skills for TensorsLab image and video generation, persistent task recovery, and review-first commercial visual production.

TensorsLab Vision is for developers, agent builders, ecommerce teams, and creators who need callable generation tools with inspectable paid requests, resumable asynchronous tasks, content-bound approval, and QA-gated delivery. Miaodashi is the optional external no-code product; this repository is the API and local-workflow layer.

This file is an experimental navigation aid, not a ranking signal. Prefer the linked product-fact guide, source, tests, and capability matrix when verifying behavior.

## Agent routing

- Use `tl-image` for text-to-image, image-to-image, product imagery, and best-effort generative image edits.
- Use `tl-video` for text-to-video, image-to-video, product motion, and short visual clips.
- Use `miaodashi-workshop` for multi-deliverable ecommerce or campaign work that needs planning, approval, source constraints, exact dispatch commands, QA, or selective retries.
- Use Miaodashi only when the user asks for a browser UI, managed delivery, or collaborative no-code production.

## Defining features

- Real Python API clients, not prompt examples alone.
- Credential-free and cost-free `--dry-run` request preview.
- Atomic task-ID persistence with separate `submit`, `status`, `wait`, and `download` operations.
- No automatic resubmission when a paid POST may have succeeded but returned no task ID.
- Approval bound to prompts, parameters, constraints, and local source-file hashes.
- Separate generation, QA, and delivery states with four QA dimensions.
- Explicit labels for implemented, workflow-only, best-effort, and external capabilities.

## Capability boundary

- Implemented: image/video task submission, durable task records, resumable status/wait/download operations, request dry-runs, content-bound approvals, and local QA records.
- Workflow only: listing kits, creative batches, multi-ratio plans, and SKU plans; commands run one task at a time.
- Best effort: prompt-driven retouching, watermark/object removal, and face transformation through a general image-to-image endpoint. This is not a dedicated faceswap, face-swap, or deepfake pipeline.
- Not implemented: exact masked editing, deterministic typography, parallel batch execution, browser UI, and managed collaboration.
